answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The forge multiplier is published, charged in cedar, and velvet lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3263 identities would post 1644 proofs and burn roughly 90 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
